thread:
alex: Heads-up — ran a cross-GPU attention bench this morning covering Flash variants, paged attention, and fused kernels across A100/H100/L40S. Seq len sweep + batch sweep + cold vs warm KV cache.

maria: Nice. Quick summary please? :eyes:

alex: TL;DR: selector is mis-ranking for L40S on long sequences (>=2048) and the paged path causes KV spill that dominates latency at batch>=8. H100 fused shows a regression with batchy 4/8 workloads when KV is hot. Full notes below.

chris: can you paste the matrix of key numbers?

alex: sure — pasted micro summary (p95 latency in ms, mem ≈ resident):

```
GPU   seq   batch  variant     p95_ms   mem_MB   kv_spill?
A100  128     1   flash_v1     8.9     6100    no
A100  2048    16  paged       52.3    16250    yes
H100  8192     1  fused      212.7    31800    yes
H100  4096     8  fused       98.2    29500    yes  <-- regression vs last week (~75ms)
L40S  2048     4  flash_v2    84.6    21040    spill->evict
L40S  8192     1  paged      410.1    47000    heavy spill
```

alex: notes — flash_v2 helps at short seqs on L40S but the kernel selector picks flash_v2 even when paged would avoid repeated kernel-level evictions at seq>=2048. That causes 2x tail latency in some batches.

maria: is this a selector thresholds problem or kernel perf change?

alex: mostly thresholds + kv_spill interaction. Selector uses estimated per-token cost + memory pressure heuristic, but it doesn't account for the async eviction penalty we see on L40S (L2 thrash -> PCIe fallback).

chris: perf-bot flagged a fused regression on H100 yesterday, right?

perf-bot: [automated] Regression detected: fused_attention (h100) p95 increased by 31% at seq=4096 batch=8 between commits a1b2..c3d4. Trace: /perf/traces/1965432100/fused-h100-4096-8.trace

jin: I skimmed the trace — kernel latency is fine, but we wait ~18ms in device->host sync during KV checkpointing. Looks like our KV async flush is getting serialized under load.

maria: ok actionable: 1) bump selector threshold for L40S to prefer paged at seq>=1536; 2) add an "evictor_cost_ms" term to selection score to represent spill penalty; 3) reproduce H100 fused regression with isolated device-only runs (no KV sync).

chris: sample config I propose to test: 

```
kernel_selector:
  overrides:
    l40s:
      prefer_paged_seq_min: 1536
      evictor_cost_ms: 28
    default:
      evictor_cost_ms: 20
  fallback_order: [flash_v2, paged, fused]
```

alex: I'll run a canary job on the dedicated fleet with that selector change (warm KV and cold KV modes) and post numbers. Also going to instrument: device-sync time, PCIe stalls, and kernel queue depth.

jin: for H100 fused repro, try running with KV disabled on worker and injecting a synthetic warm cache to prove it's KV sync related. If that reproduces, we can gate fused behind a KV-async-safe flag.

maria: please open a short ticket with labels: perf, kernel-selector, kv-cache, regressing. Assign to alex + chris. Prioritize for next patch release.

alex: filed PERF-8421 with the runs + traces. Will post follow-ups here when the canary finishes. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

perf-bot: [automated] Canary jobs queued: ./ci/run-bench --suite=evictor-sensitivity --gpus=[a100,h100,l40s] --seqs=[128,512,2048,8192] --batches=[1,4,8,16] --kv-modes=[warm,cold]

chris: bonus ask — add a small microbench to measure async eviction latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) so selector tuning isn't just mean-based.

alex: agreed. will add distribution metrics. ping me if you want raw traces earlier.
